problem: Prior navigation instruction generators (speakers) assume discrete viewpoint graphs with panoramic observations where trajectory structure is explicit; in continuous environments with only a dense egocentric RGB stream, path direction, turns and goal progress are hard to recover, and generic MLLMs produce spatially imprecise instructions.
motivation: Instruction generation is key for human-robot interaction and scalable VLN data construction, yet continuous-environment (R2R-CE/RxR-CE) speakers are unexplored. Adjacent frames look alike while motions differ, and MLLMs lack fine-grained spatial reasoning, so trajectory geometry must be supplied explicitly.
key_idea: Convert implicit trajectory geometry into explicit visual trajectory prompts (path ribbon, rotation arrow, endpoint marker) on event-selected keyframes, inject them into the ViT via a gated modulator, and calibrate the gate with RL.
insight: Explicit trajectory cues injected into the vision encoder matter most: adding VTMod gives the largest single gain in the component ablation (BLEU-4 0.288→0.308, SPICE 0.223→0.238). Gated patchwise projection at a single early layer (7) beats cross-attention and multi-layer injection, and the gate contrastive loss adds over pure GRPO (BLEU-4 0.314→0.320). Generic MLLMs, even large proprietary ones, do poorly (GPT-5.4 CIDEr 0.078), so scale alone does not solve the task.
method: EDTC (event-driven trajectory compression): action run-length encoding (long forward segments split above 4 m), small-step combo grouping (M≤6), and dynamic priority-based compression using a joint visual+geometric score to keep at most 32 keyframes (always keeping first and current frame).

VTP rendering: per-keyframe overlays of a smoothed path ribbon (Chaikin smoothing, Gaussian smoothing, occlusion check), a rotation arrow with angle for pure rotations, and an endpoint marker; stored as a 3-channel binary mask. Prompts are told to use but not mention the overlays.
GPT-based quality filtering: GPT scores candidate instructions on directional accuracy, landmark specificity, distance plausibility and fluency; only samples with score ≥6/10 are kept for training.

VTMod: a VTP Encoder (3 stride-2 conv+GN+GELU blocks with 64/128/256 channels, 1x1 conv to 384, adaptive pooling to the ViT patch grid) injected at ViT layer 7 via h' = h + g ⊙ LN(Wv), with a zero-initialised channel-wise gate g.
SFT stage: full fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-8B on an interleaved keyframe/action-text sequence with next-token cross-entropy, using a higher LR for the new VTP/VTMod parameters.

VT-GRPO: GRPO with G=8 and an NLG-metric reward (BLEU-1/4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr) plus a gate contrastive loss on the best vs worst completion (α=0.05); ViT, VTP encoder and projection are frozen, LLM and gate are trained.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (fine-tuned with SFT then VT-GRPO) plus VTP Encoder/VTMod
setting.training_data: GPT-quality-filtered (score ≥6/10) VTP-annotated trajectories from the R2R-CE and RxR-CE train splits only; SFT 3 epochs, then VT-GRPO 1 epoch
setting.observation: egocentric RGB keyframes (wide-aspect image) with rendered VTP overlay masks, plus action-displacement text; action sequence available
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, stop (used as input; the task outputs text)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth trajectory action sequence and geometry (path/goal position) are used to render the VTP overlays at test time; no nav graph, map or reconstruction. Real-world clips use estimated depth and pose.

numbers.extra: NLG metrics on generated instructions; per-sub-path aggregation following C-Instructor

numbers_note: Instruction-generation (NLG) metrics are the main results; SR/SPL rows are for downstream followers driven by generated instructions, not a navigation agent of the paper itself. Metrics 0-1 scale as printed for NLG.
results: VTInstructor achieves R2R-CE CIDEr 0.560 vs 0.203 for the best baseline (Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview), and RxR-CE CIDEr 0.142 vs under 0.033 for baselines. Its instructions drive a frozen CorrectNav follower to SR 63.3 (human instructions: 61.6; best other source Qwen3.5-Plus: 48.6), and 20K generated instructions add about +3 SR on R2R-CE and RxR-CE.
limitations: VT-GRPO rewards are only NLG metrics against references, so the policy is not directly optimised for navigational success.
Cross-setting comparison with discrete-graph speakers is not strictly controlled; the method requires the action sequence and trajectory geometry to render overlays.
Downstream evaluation uses a single frozen follower, and the real-world evaluation is small (50 clips, 3 annotators).
